html:
The first Roman emperor, who ruled from 27 BCE until his death in 14 CE. Born Gaius Octavius, he is also called Octavian.

He was the great-nephew of Julius Caesar, who adopted him in his will. At nineteen he raised an army, joined Antony and Lepidus in the Second Triumvirate, and destroyed his enemies. With his friend Agrippa in command he beat Antony and Cleopatra at Actium in 31 BCE.

In 27 BCE he took the name Augustus (see Augustus becomes first emperor). He kept the outward forms of the Republic but held the armies and the real power. His long reign brought the Pax Romana, two centuries of relative peace. He said he found Rome a city of brick and left it one of marble, and he built himself the Mausoleum of Augustus.

He pushed the frontiers to the Danube and added Egypt, but the loss of three legions at the Teutoburg Forest in 9 CE stopped him at the Rhine. His wife Livia advised him for over fifty years, and her son Tiberius succeeded him.
sum: The first Roman emperor, who ruled from 27 BCE until his death in 14 CE. Born Gaius Octavius, he is also called Octavian.
